items.headline: Woman jailed 12 years for fatally stabbing her lover in a dispute over money
items.summary: Li Ye, a Chinese national who was 37 at the time, pleaded guilty on 24 July to culpable homicide not amounting to murder after killing her lover as their relationship soured under financial strain.

items.headline: Singapore launches a five-year Youth Plan with new community 'third spaces'
items.summary: President Tharman Shanmugaratnam and Acting Culture, Community and Youth Minister David Neo launched the Youth Plan on 25 July, promising 12 new community 'third spaces' by end-2026 and S$500 'Curiosity Credits' for underprivileged youths.

items.headline: Man, 23, jailed four months over CTE midnight joyride that ended in a major crash
items.summary: A Singaporean man was among six people on a pre-dawn joyride along the Central Expressway that ended in a serious accident; he was sentenced to four months' jail.

items.headline: Man, 58, jailed after crashing a Porsche into Suntec City's Fountain of Wealth
items.summary: A driver who crashed his Porsche into the Fountain of Wealth at Suntec City was handed five weeks' jail and a 30-month driving ban.

items.headline: Update: India's youth 'Cockroach' party holds government talks but vows to keep protesting
items.summary: Leaders of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party met two senior ministers in New Delhi on 24 July over the exam paper-leak scandal, but rejected the government's draft law and refused to halt the biggest protests Prime Minister Narendra Modi has faced since 2014.

items.headline: Modi promises fast-track courts and tougher penalties over exam-paper leaks
items.summary: In a late-night video, Narendra Modi pledged special fast-track courts and stricter punishments for those behind the exam-paper leaks fuelling nationwide student protests; demonstrators dismissed the move and demanded the education minister resign.

items.headline: Congress stages a mock 'funeral' for Modi and his cabinet amid Parliament disruption
items.summary: India's Congress party held a theatrical 'funeral' for the prime minister and his ministers as opposition MPs disrupted the monsoon session of Parliament in support of the student-led protest movement.

items.headline: US-China trade war reaches India's streets as Modi weighs his Washington bet
items.summary: As Modi deepens ties with Washington amid Trump's pressure over tariffs and Russian oil, India's manufacturers remain heavily dependent on Chinese inputs, leaving Delhi caught between the two powers.

items.headline: UK private sector hits a three-month high as World Cup and heatwave lift activity
items.summary: The S&P Global flash composite PMI jumped to 52.1 in July from 49.3 in June, well above the 49.8 forecast, as a men's World Cup, staycations and hot weather boosted services and manufacturing; Middle East tensions remain a risk.

items.headline: Burnham's early 'feel-good' policies lift Labour but a hard six months loom
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham's opening moves — a bus-fare cap, cuts to electricity levies and lower duties on pubs — have brightened the mood, but analysts warn of a souring economy and rising borrowing costs ahead.

items.headline: Burnham's rebel-heavy cabinet sends a tricky message to Westminster
items.summary: Having sacked Rachel Reeves and a raft of Starmer loyalists, Burnham has assembled a cabinet of allies and former rebels, a shake-up wider than Westminster expected that signals a sharp change of direction.

items.headline: Bond markets put new Chancellor John Healey's fiscal plans to the test
items.summary: Investors and City figures, including JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon, are scrutinising John Healey after his surprise appointment as Chancellor, with UK gilts in focus as he pledges discipline under Burnham's 'new economic model.'

items.headline: Update: US halts Iran strikes as Oman brokers Hormuz talks and Houthis hit Saudi oil
items.summary: The US paused its bombing campaign for the first night in nearly two weeks while Oman mediated on reopening the Strait of Hormuz; hours later Yemen's Houthis struck Saudi Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, opening a new Red Sea front and pushing Brent crude back above $100.

items.headline: Pakistan-administered Kashmir readies for a fraught 27 July election after a violent summer
items.summary: Daily life returned to Muzaffarabad as Pakistan-administered Kashmir prepared to vote on 27 July, following months of deadly protests, road closures and internet curbs across the region.

items.headline: France becomes the first EU country to ban social media for under-15s
items.summary: Both chambers of France's parliament approved a ban on social-media access for children under 15, a flagship reform of President Macron's second term modelled on Australia's under-16 ban, to be enforced from September.

items.headline: Nicaragua's Ortega declares there will be 'no more elections'
items.summary: President Daniel Ortega said Nicaragua will no longer hold elections, scrapping a vote due in 2027 and further entrenching the rule he shares with his wife Rosario Murillo after nearly two decades in power.

items.headline: OpenAI's spending forecast balloons to $750bn as it unveils a self-built data centre
items.summary: OpenAI raised its projected compute spending through 2030 to roughly $750 billion and announced 'Project Camellia,' a $20 billion-plus, 3.2-gigawatt data-centre campus in Effingham County, Georgia — the first it will design and build itself.

items.headline: Meta, Microsoft and Amazon face investor unease over AI spending as earnings loom
items.summary: After Alphabet lifted its 2026 capital-spending guidance, Wall Street is pressing Big Tech on whether roughly $725 billion in combined AI investment this year will pay off; Microsoft is coming off its worst month since 2000.

items.headline: Alphabet lifts its 2026 AI capital-spending guidance to as much as $205bn
items.summary: Google parent Alphabet raised its full-year capital-expenditure forecast to $195-$205 billion, up from $180-$190 billion, with most of the money going toward data centres and compute to keep pace in the AI race.

items.headline: Warner Bros Discovery and Paramount agree to pause their $110bn merger
items.summary: Paramount Skydance agreed to postpone closing its takeover of Warner Bros Discovery until a state antitrust case is resolved or June 2027, extending a federal judge's pause after 12 states sued to block the deal.

items.headline: Corporate profits beat a high bar, yet traders still aren't impressed
items.summary: About 85% of S&P 500 companies reporting so far have topped profit estimates — the highest share in five years — but the median stock has failed to outperform the index the day after results.

items.headline: Oil seen ending 2026 near $100 as Middle East disruptions persist
items.summary: Consultancy Rapidan forecast Brent crude will finish the year around $100 a barrel as war in the Gulf keeps supply routes at risk, even after Friday's near-4% slide on hopes of revived US-Iran talks.

items.headline: 🏎️ Norris snatches a dramatic Hungarian GP pole from Hamilton by 0.012s
items.summary: McLaren's Lando Norris pipped Lewis Hamilton to pole at the Hungaroring by just twelve thousandths of a second for his first pole of 2026, as Max Verstappen spun in Q3.

items.headline: 🏎️ Hamilton demoted to fifth by a grid penalty, promoting Leclerc to the front row
items.summary: Stewards handed Hamilton a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri in qualifying, dropping the Ferrari driver from second to fifth and lifting team-mate Charles Leclerc onto the front row alongside Norris.

items.headline: 🏏 India crush Zimbabwe by 90 runs to seal the T20I series with a game to spare
items.summary: Ishan Kishan (81) and Tilak Varma (60) powered India to 219 for 5, then the bowlers bundled Zimbabwe out for 129 in Harare, giving Shreyas Iyer's side an unassailable 2-0 lead; Kishan was named player of the match.

items.headline: 🎾 Halys stuns defending champion Bublik to win his maiden ATP title at Kitzbuhel
items.summary: France's Quentin Halys beat defending champion Alexander Bublik 6-4, 7-6(6) in the Kitzbuhel final to claim the first ATP Tour title of his career.

items.headline: NASA's Psyche probe returns its first Mars flyby data en route to a metal-rich asteroid
items.summary: NASA's Psyche spacecraft used a gravity assist at Mars for a roughly 1,000 mph boost and has returned its first flyby imagery and a time-lapse video, keeping it on course to reach the metal asteroid Psyche in 2029.

items.headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope clears a solar-panel checkout ahead of launch
items.summary: Engineers at Kennedy Space Center completed prelaunch cleaning and inspection of the solar panels that will power NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, a wide-field observatory built to probe dark energy and exoplanets.

items.headline: NASA's Webb reveals an exoplanet whose helium-and-carbon atmosphere defies explanation
items.summary: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope observed a Jupiter-mass world with an exotic helium- and carbon-dominated atmosphere unlike any seen before, challenging existing models of how such planets form.

items.headline: NASA's Webb finds a black hole that formed before its host galaxy
items.summary: Observations with the James Webb Space Telescope point to a supermassive black hole that appears to predate the galaxy around it, offering fresh clues to how the universe's earliest giant black holes grew so quickly.

fun_fact.headline: How honeybees dance directions to their hive
fun_fact.body: A foraging honeybee tells its hivemates exactly where to find food by performing a 'waggle dance': a figure-eight run whose angle relative to vertical encodes the food's direction relative to the Sun, and whose duration encodes the distance. Decoding this dance language earned Austrian ethologist Karl von Frisch a share of the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. It is one of the few known cases of a non-human animal communicating abstract, symbolic information.

puzzle.title: A Perfect Shot
puzzle.body:
A woman walks up to her husband and shoots him. Then she holds him under water for a full minute. A few hours later, the two of them head out and enjoy a pleasant dinner together.
How is this possible?
puzzle.approach: Every word can carry more than one meaning — question the violent-sounding ones.
puzzle.answer:
She is a photographer. She 'shot' her husband with a camera — took his photograph — then developed the print by holding it in a tray of water, part of the old chemical film-developing process. With the photo finished, the couple simply went out to dinner.
The trick is that 'shoots' and 'holds him under water' both sound violent but describe ordinary steps in film photography.

word_puzzle.title: Table Manners
word_puzzle.body:
Centre letter:  T
Outer letters:  A · B · E · L · N · O

Make as many words (4+ letters) as you can. Every word must contain the centre letter T and use only these seven letters; letters may repeat. One word — the pangram — uses all seven at least once.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must include the centre letter T and use only the seven letters (letters may repeat). One word uses all seven.
word_puzzle.answer:
Pangram: NOTABLE.
Other valid words include: TABLE, TALE, LATE, TEAL, TALON, TONAL, ATONE, NOTE, TONE, TOTE, TOTAL, LOTTO, BATON, BEAT, BLEAT, BLOAT, NEAT, ELATE, OBLATE, BATTLE, BEATEN, BOTTLE.
(Any other real words you found that contain T and use only A, B, E, L, N, O, T count too.)
